184	    ):
185	        """Init ModelLightningModule with key parameters.
186	
187	        Args:
188	            model: Which type of the model for training
189	            include_line_graph: whether to include line graphs
190	            data_mean: average of training data
191	            data_std: standard deviation of training data
192	            loss: loss function used for training
193	            loss_params: parameters for loss function
194	            optimizer: optimizer for training
195	            scheduler: scheduler for training
196	            lr: learning rate for training
197	            decay_steps: number of steps for decaying learning rate
198	            decay_alpha: parameter determines the minimum learning rate.
199	            sync_dist: whether sync logging across all GPU workers or not
200	            **kwargs: Passthrough to parent init.
201	        """
202	        super().__init__(**kwargs)
203	
204	        self.model = model
205	        self.include_line_graph = include_line_graph
206	        self.mae = torchmetrics.MeanAbsoluteError()
207	        self.rmse = torchmetrics.MeanSquaredError(squared=False)
208	        self.data_mean = data_mean
209	        self.data_std = data_std
210	        self.lr = lr
211	        self.decay_steps = decay_steps
212	        self.decay_alpha = decay_alpha
213	        if loss == "mse_loss":
214	            self.loss = F.mse_loss
215	        elif loss == "huber_loss":
216	            self.loss = F.huber_loss  # type:ignore[assignment]
217	        elif loss == "smooth_l1_loss":
218	            self.loss = F.smooth_l1_loss  # type:ignore[assignment]
219	        else:
220	            self.loss = F.l1_loss
221	        self.optimizer = optimizer
222	        self.scheduler = scheduler
223	        self.sync_dist = sync_dist
224	        self.loss_params = loss_params if loss_params is not None else {}

226	        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=["model", "optimizer", "scheduler"])

228	    def forward(
229	        self,
230	        g: Any,
231	        lat: torch.Tensor | None = None,
232	        l_g: Any = None,
233	        state_attr: torch.Tensor | None = None,
234	    ):
235	        """Run the wrapped model.
236	
237	        Attaches per-node ``pos`` and per-edge ``pbc_offshift`` tensors derived from
238	        ``frac_coords`` / ``pbc_offset`` and the supplied lattice(s), then delegates
239	        to the wrapped model.
240	
241	        Args:
242	            g: PyG ``Data``/``Batch`` graph.
243	            lat: Lattice tensor. ``(3, 3)`` for a single graph or ``(B, 3, 3)`` when batched.
244	            l_g: Optional line graph.
245	            state_attr: Optional state attribute.
246	
247	        Returns:
248	            Model prediction.
249	        """
250	        if lat is not None:
251	            if lat.dim() == 2:
252	                lat = lat.unsqueeze(0)
253	            batch = getattr(g, "batch", None)
254	            if batch is None:
255	                batch = torch.zeros(g.num_nodes, dtype=torch.long, device=g.frac_coords.device)
256	            node_lat = lat[batch]
257	            g.pos = (g.frac_coords.unsqueeze(dim=-1) * node_lat).sum(dim=1)
258	            edge_lat = lat[batch[g.edge_index[0]]]
259	            g.pbc_offshift = (g.pbc_offset.unsqueeze(dim=-1) * edge_lat).sum(dim=1)
260	        if self.include_line_graph:
261	            return self.model(g=g, l_g=l_g, state_attr=state_attr)
262	        return self.model(g, state_attr=state_attr)
263	
264	    def step(self, batch: tuple) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], int]:
265	        """Run a single training/validation step.
266	
267	        Args:
268	            batch: Batch of training data.
269	
270	        Returns:
271	            results, batch_size
272	        """
273	        if self.include_line_graph:
274	            g, lat, l_g, state_attr, labels = batch
275	            preds = self(g=g, lat=lat, l_g=l_g, state_attr=state_attr)
276	        else:
277	            g, lat, state_attr, labels = batch
278	            preds = self(g=g, lat=lat, state_attr=state_attr)
279	        results = self.loss_fn(loss=self.loss, preds=preds, labels=labels)  # type: ignore
280	        batch_size = preds.numel()
281	        return results, batch_size
282	
283	    def loss_fn(self, loss: nn.Module, labels: torch.Tensor, preds: torch.Tensor) -> dict[str, Any]:
284	        """Compute training loss and metrics.
285	
286	        Args:
287	            loss: Loss function.
288	            labels: Labels to compute the loss.
289	            preds: Predictions.
290	
291	        Returns:
292	            {"Total_Loss": total_loss, "MAE": mae, "RMSE": rmse}
293	        """
294	        scaled_pred = torch.reshape(preds * self.data_std + self.data_mean, labels.size())
295	        total_loss = loss(labels, scaled_pred, **self.loss_params)
296	        mae = self.mae(labels, scaled_pred)
297	        rmse = self.rmse(labels, scaled_pred)
298	        return {"Total_Loss": total_loss, "MAE": mae, "RMSE": rmse}

459

461	            batch: Batch of training data.
462	
463	        Returns:
464	            results, batch_size
465	        """
466	        preds: tuple
467	        labels: tuple

469	        torch.set_grad_enabled(True)
470	        # Batch shape is fully determined by ``include_line_graph``:
471	        #   line graph: (g, lat, l_g, state_attr, energies, forces, stresses, [extra])
472	        #   otherwise:  (g, lat,      state_attr, energies, forces, stresses, [extra])
473	        # where the trailing optional ``extra`` is magmoms (calc_magmom) or
474	        # charges (calc_charge); ``forward`` mirrors the optional with an
475	        # extra return slot. ``preds`` is just the forward output with the
476	        # hessian (index 3) dropped, then a ``squeeze`` on the charge slot
477	        # to match the legacy shape contract.
478	        if self.include_line_graph:
479	            g, lat, l_g, state_attr, *targets = batch
480	            out = self(g=g, lat=lat, state_attr=state_attr, l_g=l_g)
481	        else:
482	            g, lat, state_attr, *targets = batch
483	            out = self(g=g, lat=lat, state_attr=state_attr)
484	
485	        preds = (out[0], out[1], out[2], *out[4:])
486	        labels = tuple(targets)
487	        if self.model.calc_charge:
488	            preds = (preds[0], preds[1], preds[2], preds[3].squeeze())
489	            labels = (labels[0], labels[1], labels[2], labels[3].squeeze())
490	
491	        num_atoms = torch.bincount(g.batch)
492	        results = self.loss_fn(
493	            loss=self.loss,  # type: ignore
494	            preds=preds,
495	            labels=labels,
496	            num_atoms=num_atoms,
497	        )
498	        batch_size = preds[0].numel()
499	
500	        self._last_preds = preds
501	        self._last_labels = labels
502	        self._last_num_atoms = num_atoms
503	        self._last_indices = getattr(g, "sample_idx", None)
504	
505	        return results, batch_size

550	    def loss_fn(
551	        self,
552	        loss: nn.Module,
553	        labels: tuple,
554	        preds: tuple,
555	        num_atoms: torch.Tensor | None = None,
556	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
557	        """Compute losses for EFS.
558	
559	        Args:
560	            loss: Loss function.
561	            labels: Labels.
562	            preds: Predictions
563	            num_atoms: Number of atoms.
564	
565	        Returns::
566	
567	            {
568	                "Total_Loss": total_loss,
569	                "Energy_MAE": e_mae,
570	                "Force_MAE": f_mae,
571	                "Stress_MAE": s_mae,
572	                "Magmom_MAE": m_mae,
573	                "Charge_MAE": q_mae,
574	                "Energy_RMSE": e_rmse,
575	                "Force_RMSE": f_rmse,
576	                "Stress_RMSE": s_rmse,
577	                "Magmom_RMSE": m_rmse,
578	                "Charge_RMSE": q_rmse
579	            }
580	
581	        """
582	        # labels and preds are (energy, force, stress, (optional) site_wise)
583	        if num_atoms is None:
584	            num_atoms = torch.ones_like(preds[0])
585	        if self.allow_missing_labels:
586	            valid_labels, valid_preds = [], []
587	            for index, label in enumerate(labels):
588	                valid_value_indices = ~torch.isnan(label)
589	                valid_labels.append(label[valid_value_indices])
590	                if index == 0:
591	                    valid_num_atoms = num_atoms[valid_value_indices]
592	                    pred = preds[index].view(1) if preds[index].shape == torch.Size([]) else preds[index]
593	                else:
594	                    pred = preds[index]
595	                valid_preds.append(pred[valid_value_indices])
596	        else:
597	            valid_labels, valid_preds = list(labels), list(preds)
598	            valid_num_atoms = num_atoms
599	
600	        # Per-atom energies are reused three times (loss, MAE, RMSE) — hoist
601	        # the divisions out of the metric calls so each tensor is materialised
602	        # once per loss_fn invocation.
603	        e_label_per_atom = valid_labels[0] / valid_num_atoms
604	        e_pred_per_atom = valid_preds[0] / valid_num_atoms
605	
606	        e_loss = self.loss(e_label_per_atom, e_pred_per_atom, **self.loss_params)
607	        f_loss = self.loss(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1], **self.loss_params)
608	
609	        e_mae = self.mae(e_label_per_atom, e_pred_per_atom)
610	        f_mae = self.mae(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1])
611	
612	        e_rmse = self.rmse(e_label_per_atom, e_pred_per_atom)
613	        f_rmse = self.rmse(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1])
614	
615	        s_mae = torch.zeros(1)
616	        s_rmse = torch.zeros(1)
617	
618	        m_mae = torch.zeros(1)
619	        m_rmse = torch.zeros(1)
620	
621	        q_mae = torch.zeros(1)
622	        q_rmse = torch.zeros(1)
623	
624	        total_loss = self.energy_weight * e_loss + self.force_weight * f_loss
625	
626	        if self.model.calc_stresses:
627	            s_loss = loss(valid_labels[2], valid_preds[2], **self.loss_params)
628	            s_mae = self.mae(valid_labels[2], valid_preds[2])
629	            s_rmse = self.rmse(valid_labels[2], valid_preds[2])
630	            total_loss = total_loss + self.stress_weight * s_loss
631	
632	        if self.model.calc_magmom and labels[3].numel() > 0:
633	            if self.magmom_target == "symbreak":
634	                # Each metric was being recomputed twice for the +/- predictions; cache
635	                # the four tensors and pick the per-element minimum at the end.
636	                neg_pred = -valid_preds[3]
637	                m_loss = torch.min(
638	                    loss(valid_labels[3], valid_preds[3], **self.loss_params),
639	                    loss(valid_labels[3], neg_pred, **self.loss_params),
640	                )
641	                m_mae = torch.min(self.mae(valid_labels[3], valid_preds[3]), self.mae(valid_labels[3], neg_pred))
642	                m_rmse = torch.min(self.rmse(valid_labels[3], valid_preds[3]), self.rmse(valid_labels[3], neg_pred))
643	            else:
644	                labels_3 = torch.abs(valid_labels[3]) if self.magmom_target == "absolute" else valid_labels[3]
645	                m_loss = loss(labels_3, valid_preds[3], **self.loss_params)
646	                m_mae = self.mae(labels_3, valid_preds[3])
647	                m_rmse = self.rmse(labels_3, valid_preds[3])
648	            total_loss = total_loss + self.magmom_weight * m_loss
649	
650	        if self.model.calc_charge:
651	            q_loss = loss(labels[3], preds[3])
652	            q_mae = self.mae(labels[3], preds[3])
653	            q_rmse = self.rmse(labels[3], preds[3])
654	            total_loss = total_loss + self.charge_weight * q_loss
655	
656	        return {
657	            "Total_Loss": total_loss,
658	            "Energy_MAE": e_mae,
659	            "Force_MAE": f_mae,
660	            "Stress_MAE": s_mae,
661	            "Magmom_MAE": m_mae,
662	            "Charge_MAE": q_mae,
663	            "Energy_RMSE": e_rmse,
664	            "Force_RMSE": f_rmse,
665	            "Stress_RMSE": s_rmse,
666	            "Magmom_RMSE": m_rmse,
667	            "Charge_RMSE": q_rmse,
668	        }

671	def fit_element_refs(
672	    structures: Iterable[Structure],
673	    energies: ArrayLike,
674	    element_types: Sequence[str],
675	    *,
676	    rcond: float | None = None,
677	) -> np.ndarray:
678	    r"""Fit per-element energy offsets via linear regression.
679	
680	    Solves the least-squares problem
681	
682	    .. math::
683	
684	        E_i \approx \sum_{Z \in S} \mu_Z \, N_{i,Z}
685	
686	    where :math:`E_i` is the total energy of structure :math:`i`,
687	    :math:`N_{i,Z}` is the count of element :math:`Z` in that structure,
688	    and :math:`\mu_Z` is the per-element offset returned in the same
689	    order as ``element_types``. The result is shaped to drop straight
690	    into :class:`PotentialLightningModule` or
691	    :class:`matgl.apps.pes.Potential` as ``element_refs``.
692	
693	    Subtracting these offsets from the targets removes the (usually
694	    dominant) constant-per-element contribution from the loss so the
695	    model only has to learn the relative-energy surface. This stabilises
696	    training when the absolute energy scale (~tens of eV per atom) is
697	    large compared to the residual variation across a chemically
698	    homogeneous training set.
699	
700	    Args:
701	        structures: Iterable of pymatgen ``Structure`` (or ``Molecule``)
702	            objects. Composition is read via ``site.specie.symbol``.
703	        energies: Total potential energies, one per structure, in any
704	            unit consistent with downstream training (usually eV).
705	        element_types: Element ordering used by the model — typically
706	            the value of ``model.element_types`` or what
707	            ``matgl.ext.pymatgen.get_element_list`` returns. The output
708	            offset vector is in this order.
709	        rcond: Forwarded to ``numpy.linalg.lstsq``. ``None`` (default)
710	            uses NumPy's current default cutoff for small singular
711	            values; pass ``-1`` to retain old behaviour, or a float to
712	            override.
713	
714	    Returns:
715	        ``np.ndarray`` of shape ``(len(element_types),)`` with the fitted
716	        per-element offsets, dtype ``float64``.
717	
718	    Raises:
719	        ValueError: If ``structures`` and ``energies`` have different
720	            lengths, or if a structure contains an element not listed in
721	            ``element_types``.
722	
723	    Note:
724	        For inputs already in graph form (e.g. an
725	        :class:`~matgl.graph.data.MGLDataset` of PyG ``Data``
726	        objects), :meth:`matgl.layers.AtomRef.fit` provides the same
727	        regression directly on the layer.
728	
729	    Example:
730	        >>> from matgl.ext.pymatgen import get_element_list
731	        >>> elements = get_element_list(structures)
732	        >>> refs = fit_element_refs(structures, energies, elements)
733	        >>> module = PotentialLightningModule(model=model, element_refs=refs)
734	    """
735	    element_types = tuple(element_types)
736	    if not element_types:
737	        raise ValueError("element_types must be non-empty.")
738	
739	    z_to_col = {sym: i for i, sym in enumerate(element_types)}
740	    structures_list = list(structures)
741	    energies_arr = np.asarray(energies, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
742	
743	    if len(structures_list) != energies_arr.shape[0]:
744	        raise ValueError(
745	            f"len(structures)={len(structures_list)} does not match len(energies)={energies_arr.shape[0]}."
746	        )
747	    if not structures_list:
748	        raise ValueError("structures must be non-empty.")
749	
750	    counts = np.zeros((len(structures_list), len(element_types)), dtype=np.float64)
751	    for i, struct in enumerate(structures_list):
752	        for site in struct:
753	            sym = site.specie.symbol
754	            col = z_to_col.get(sym)
755	            if col is None:
756	                raise ValueError(
757	                    f"Structure {i} contains element {sym!r} which is not in element_types={element_types}."
758	                )
759	            counts[i, col] += 1.0
760	
761	    refs, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(counts, energies_arr, rcond=rcond)
762	    return refs

765	def xavier_init(model: nn.Module, gain: float = 1.0, distribution: Literal["uniform", "normal"] = "uniform") -> None:
766	    """Xavier initialization scheme for the model.
767	
768	    Args:
769	        model (nn.Module): The model to be Xavier-initialized.
770	        gain (float): Gain factor. Defaults to 1.0.
771	        distribution (Literal["uniform", "normal"], optional): Distribution to use. Defaults to "uniform".
772	    """
773	    if distribution == "uniform":
774	        init_fn = nn.init.xavier_uniform_
775	    elif distribution == "normal":
776	        init_fn = nn.init.xavier_normal_
777	    else:
778	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid distribution: {distribution}")
779	
780	    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
781	        if name.endswith(".bias"):
782	            param.data.fill_(0)
783	        elif param.dim() < 2:  # torch.nn.xavier only supports >= 2 dim tensors
784	            bound = gain * math.sqrt(6) / math.sqrt(2 * param.shape[0])
785	            if distribution == "uniform":
786	                param.data.uniform_(-bound, bound)
787	            else:
788	                param.data.normal_(0, bound**2)
789	        else:
790	            init_fn(param.data, gain=gain)

882	def _matpes_samples_to_lists(
883	    samples: Iterable[Mapping],
884	    stress_unit: StressUnit = "kbar",
885	    *,
886	    include_charges: bool | ChargesSource = False,
887	    include_magmoms: bool | MagmomsSource = False,
888	) -> tuple[list[Structure], dict[str, list]]:
889	    """Walk a MatPES sample list and return parallel structures + labels dict.
890	
891	    Always extracts ``energies``, ``forces``, and ``stresses``. Per-atom optional
892	    partial-charge / magmom fields are extracted when the corresponding
893	    ``include_*`` flag is truthy; samples whose requested optional field is
894	    ``None`` (i.e. the upstream calculation failed) are dropped from every
895	    parallel list, so the returned lists stay aligned.
896	
897	    Args:
898	        samples: Iterable of MatPES sample dicts.
899	        stress_unit: On-disk stress unit; see :meth:`MGLDatasetLoader.from_json`.
900	        include_charges: If truthy, extract per-atom partial charges under the
901	            label key ``"charges"`` and drop samples with missing values.
902	            ``True`` selects DDEC6 net atomic charges
903	            (``ddec6.partial_charges``, the matgl default for QET-style
904	            training); pass ``"bader"`` for Bader electron counts
905	            (``bader_charges``) or ``"cm5"`` for CM5 charges
906	            (``cm5_partial_charges``).
907	        include_magmoms: If truthy, extract per-atom magnetic moments under
908	            ``"magmoms"`` and drop samples with missing values. ``True``
909	            selects DDEC6 spin moments (``ddec6.spin_moments``); pass
910	            ``"bader"`` for Bader magmoms (``bader_magmoms``).
911	
912	    Returns:
913	        ``(structures, labels)`` where ``labels`` has keys ``"energies"``,
914	        ``"forces"``, ``"stresses"``, and optionally ``"charges"`` / ``"magmoms"``.
915	    """
916	    # (display_name, extractor_callable) tuples, one per enabled optional.
917	    enabled: list[tuple[str, str, Any]] = []
918	    charges_resolved = _resolve_optional_source(include_charges, "charges", _CHARGES_EXTRACTORS, "ddec6")
919	    if charges_resolved is not None:
920	        enabled.append(("charges", *charges_resolved))
921	    magmoms_resolved = _resolve_optional_source(include_magmoms, "magmoms", _MAGMOMS_EXTRACTORS, "ddec6")
922	    if magmoms_resolved is not None:
923	        enabled.append(("magmoms", *magmoms_resolved))
924	
925	    structures: list[Structure] = []
926	    energies: list[float] = []
927	    forces: list = []
928	    stresses: list = []
929	    optional_lists: dict[str, list] = {label: [] for label, _, _ in enabled}
930	    factor = _STRESS_UNIT_TO_GPA[stress_unit]
931	    dropped = 0
932	
933	    for raw in samples:
934	        # Skip samples missing any requested optional field. We check before
935	        # appending anything to keep the parallel lists in lockstep.
936	        skip = False
937	        optional_values: dict[str, list] = {}
938	        for label, _src_name, extractor in enabled:
939	            value = extractor(raw)
940	            if value is None:
941	                skip = True
942	                break
943	            optional_values[label] = np.asarray(value, dtype="float64").tolist()
944	        if skip:
945	            dropped += 1
946	            continue
947	
948	        struct = raw["structure"]
949	        if not isinstance(struct, Structure):
950	            struct = Structure.from_dict(struct)
951	        structures.append(struct)
952	        energies.append(float(raw["energy"]))
953	        forces.append(np.asarray(raw["forces"], dtype="float64").tolist())
954	        stresses.append((np.asarray(raw["stress"], dtype="float64") * factor).tolist())
955	        for label, val in optional_values.items():
956	            optional_lists[label].append(val)
957	
958	    labels: dict[str, list] = {"energies": energies, "forces": forces, "stresses": stresses, **optional_lists}
959	    if dropped and enabled:
960	        import warnings
961	
962	        missing = ", ".join(f"{label}({src})" for label, src, _ in enabled)
963	        warnings.warn(
964	            f"Dropped {dropped} MatPES samples missing one of: {missing}.",
965	            UserWarning,
966	            stacklevel=2,
967	        )
968	    return structures, labels

234	    if "charges" in labels:

43

45	            structure: Input crystal or molecule (Pymatgen structure, molecule, or ASE atoms).
46	            src_id: Site indices for starting point of bonds.
47	            dst_id: Site indices for destination point of bonds.
48	            images: Periodic image offsets for the bonds.

50	            element_types: Element symbols of all atoms in the structure.

52	            is_atoms: Whether the input structure is an ASE Atoms object.
53	
54	        Returns:
55	            Tuple containing:
56	            - Data: PyTorch Geometric Data object with edge_index, node features, and edge attributes.
57	            - torch.Tensor: Lattice matrix.
58	            - np.ndarray: State attributes.
59	        """

61	        src_id = torch.as_tensor(src_id, dtype=matgl.int_th)
62	        dst_id = torch.as_tensor(dst_id, dtype=matgl.int_th)

66
